s1.syndrome_frame: Progressive neurological disorder with autonomic dysfunction and cognitive decline
key_facts: 3-year history of progressive disorder
Denies paresthesias, dysesthesias, or loss of sensation
Abnormal cardiac parasympathetic function without orthostatic hypotension
Patchy decrease in sweat output on quantitative sudomotor axon reflex test
Near complete global anhidrosis on thermoregulatory sweat test
Low α-galactosidase activity (0.056 U/L)
Elevated protein levels in cerebrospinal fluid (95 mg/dL)
No pleocytosis in cerebrospinal fluid
Bilateral hyperintensity in the pulvinar region of thalami on MRI Brain
Global diffuse brain volume loss on MRI Brain
Positive for pseudo-α-galactosidase allele
Mild neurocognitive and memory deficits on neuropsychological testing

shortlist.label: Multiple System Atrophy
shortlist.why_kept: Progressive neurological disorder with autonomic dysfunction and cognitive decline

shortlist.label: Fabry Disease
shortlist.why_kept: Low α-galactosidase activity and progressive neurological disorder

shortlist.label: Frontotemporal Dementia
shortlist.why_kept: Cognitive decline and global diffuse brain volume loss

shortlist.label: Late-Onset Tay-Sachs Disease
shortlist.why_kept: Progressive neurological disorder and positive for pseudo-α-galactosidase allele

shortlist.label: Adult Polyglucosan Body Disease
shortlist.why_kept: Progressive neurological disorder with autonomic dysfunction and cognitive decline

raw.rationale: The combination of progressive disorder, autonomic dysfunction (abnormal cardiac parasympathetic function, patchy decrease in sweat output, and near complete global anhidrosis), generalized ataxia, and cognitive decline without significant sensory symptoms aligns closely with Multiple System Atrophy. Additionally, the imaging findings of bilateral hyperintensity in the pulvinar region of thalami and global diffuse brain volume loss support this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Fabry Disease
rejected.why: Low α-galactosidase activity is consistent with Fabry Disease, but the absence of paresthesias, dysesthesias, or loss of sensation and the specific pattern of autonomic dysfunction and imaging findings make it less likely.

rejected.label: Frontotemporal Dementia
rejected.why: While cognitive decline is present, the prominent autonomic dysfunction and ataxia are not typical of Frontotemporal Dementia.

rejected.label: Late-Onset Tay-Sachs Disease
rejected.why: This condition typically presents with motor symptoms and cognitive decline, but the autonomic dysfunction and specific imaging findings in this case do not align with Late-Onset Tay-Sachs Disease.

rejected.label: Adult Polyglucosan Body Disease
rejected.why: This condition involves progressive upper and lower motor neuron impairment and dementia, which does not fully match the combination of symptoms and findings in this case, particularly the prominent autonomic features.
